candidate_relations.reason: A right thyroid mass after multiply recurrent inguinal DFSP, with pulmonary nodules, is metastatic dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, the same tumor named by the reference.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: metastatic state of the same DFSP

candidate_relations.reason: The truncated list of renal, breast, GI, lung, or melanoma metastases conflicts with a documented recurrent DFSP primary.
Thyroid lymphoma is a primary lymphoid thyroid malignancy, not FNA of a hemorrhagic mass in a patient with recurrent DFSP.
Intact PTH is normal and there is no calcitonin-producing thyroid phenotype to support medullary carcinoma over metastatic DFSP.
Papillary thyroid cancer is a primary thyroid epithelial tumor, whereas FNA showed pleomorphic nuclei in a patient with known DFSP and lung nodules.
Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans is the reference tumor, here presenting as a new thyroid mass after four inguinal recurrences.
Metastatic thyroid tumor from dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans names the same DFSP now replacing the right thyroid lobe.
Metastatic dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans to the thyroid is the same diagnostic object given the 6-cm right-lobe mass and pulmonary nodules.
Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans metastasis to the thyroid restates that the voluminous right-lobe mass is DFSP rather than a new thyroid primary.
Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is a primary undifferentiated thyroid cancer, not expected with freely mobile cords and a DFSP history.
Thyroid nodule describes the 6 × 4 × 6 cm right-lobe mass but not its DFSP identity.
The truncated differential stating metastasis from known DFSP is the same conclusion as dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans involving thyroid.
Metastatic disease to the thyroid is anatomically correct but omits dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans as the source.
Primary thyroid malignancy conflicts with a secondary DFSP deposit and pulmonary nodules after recurrent inguinal DFSP.
Radiotherapy was 66 Gy to the inguinal–suprapubic field, not the neck, so radiation-induced thyroid disease is not the mechanism.
Thyroid metastasis from another primary cancer assigns the wrong source despite the well-documented DFSP history.
Medullary thyroid cancer is unsupported by the near-normal TSH/FT4 profile and DFSP-linked lung nodules.
'None' does not name the DFSP that explains the FNA-suspicious thyroid mass.
Anaplastic thyroid cancer would typically be rapidly locally invasive; laryngoscopy showed mobile cords and the history points to DFSP.
Primary thyroid lymphoma is a distinct lymphoid primary, not hemorrhagic FNA in recurrent DFSP with lung metastases.

case_quality_flags: FNA is only suspicious for malignancy; thyroid histopathology confirming DFSP is not in the record.
